### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47a8b588207621724d85647576c4277979c253f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5912bf70cdc51ea3fe9c45939a626113eafe1b5d` — the merge of head `87e98178acf4f8fa1037a53f438a3891d50f07c5` into base `47a8b588207621724d85647576c4277979c253f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5912bf70cdc51ea3fe9c45939a626113eafe1b5d && git checkout 5912bf70cdc51ea3fe9c45939a626113eafe1b5d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 47a8b588207621724d85647576c4277979c253f7 87e98178acf4f8fa1037a53f438a3891d50f07c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 47a8b588207621724d85647576c4277979c253f7 && git merge --no-ff 87e98178acf4f8fa1037a53f438a3891d50f07c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47a8b588207621724d85647576c4277979c253f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `87e98178acf4f8fa1037a53f438a3891d50f07c5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolLabels-locale-parity-7481.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolLabels-sentences-12724.test.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/{ar,de,en,es,fr,ja,ko,pt,ru,zh}.ts

Source of the work: the PR names no in-repo card. Its source is the cloud repository's issue cloud#3383, which is not readable from this seat; the ruling it carries is judged from the PR body and from in-repo issue #28104 (the console card for the same hand-off, which restates the ruling and the "AI drafts, a person saves, never auto-submitted" scope). The rest of the diff outside `Scope:` (the two changesets) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; ② below reads them only to judge the semver level.

### ① Derived judgments

- `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']` gains `draft_record`, inserted between `describe_object` and `get_active_package`. Right: the group's sort invariant (`platform-tool-names.test.ts`, "each group is sorted") holds, the name is snake_case, collides with no other group and sits in no `action_` family namespace, so every invariant pin in the spec's own test holds on the head. Test Core is green on the head.
- `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` (the flattened set, a published const) gains one member. Right: this is the only public-surface change; no export is added or removed, so `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` are unchanged and the TypeScript Type Check job (which runs every generated-artifact gate) is green.
- Accept set of `skill.tools[]` under ADR-0109 widens by one name: `validateAiToolReferences` resolves against `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` at ladder step 2 (`collectToolUniverse`), so a skill naming `draft_record` stops being reported as `ai-skill-tool-unresolved`. Right, and pinned in the diff: the new lint case resolves `draft_record` and keeps reporting the control `draft_records` at `skills[0].tools[1]`, the same shape as the #16512 and #27002 pins beside it. Lint and Test Core are green.
- MCP bridge: `worldAnnotation()` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` now answers `openWorldHint: false` for a bridged tool named `draft_record`. Right: the registry is the ownership source by design (a platform tool acts on the environment's own records and metadata; a record draft of this stack's object is exactly that). The partial safety sets `PLATFORM_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` and `PLATFORM_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL_NAMES` are untouched, so `draft_record` gets no readOnly or destructive hint, the protocol's "unknown" default; this matches its siblings `suggest_builder` and `open_record`, which are also absent from both sets, and the registry-driven pin ("no tool outside PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES receives a hint it did not declare") iterates the widened set and stays green.
- Chatbot step label: `toolLabels-locale-parity-7481` reads `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` from the workspace spec (`@objectstack/spec: workspace:^` in `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/package.json`), so the coverage set grows by `draft_record` the moment the registry does, and every one of the ten packs must carry `chatbot.tool.draft_record`. Right: at the head all ten packs carry the key once, inside `chatbot.tool` (confirmed by reading each pack at the head, not the hunk context alone). `toolLabels-sentences-12724` requires every value to differ from the id and from the title-caser's output (`Draft record` for this id): `Draft the new record` and its nine siblings all differ, and the key set is identical across packs. Test UI is green on all 16 shards.
- No other consumer enumerates the group by hand: `ui/scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` declares `chatbot.tool.` as external vocabulary pinned by the parity test; `mapMessages.ts` names only `visualize_data`; `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` and ADR-0109 point at the file rather than listing names; no `content/docs` page lists the service-ai-studio tools. Nothing drifts.
- The group's TSDoc now says the `ask` agent's hand-off signals (`suggest_builder`, `open_record`, `draft_record`) live in this group and "write nothing". Right as a correction: the two older signals were already listed here and the previous sentence did not account for them. The "write nothing" claim for `draft_record` is held against the PR body and #28104 (the draft is validated server-side and saved by the person; never auto-submitted); its enforcement is the cloud conformance test and the cloud tool itself, not this repo (see ③).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/cloud-3383-draft-record-tool-name.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, both line-initial. Right: a new accepted `skill.tools[]` value is `added` under AGENTS.md's declaration rule, and a kind takes at least minor on the package the diff moves. The same reading landed in #27011 for cloud#3335 (the precedent the PR names). The lint rule is advisory, so the alternative reading (`none`, patch) is arguable, but it would under-declare a change whose whole purpose is to widen the accept set the lint rule enforces; minor is the direction that cannot under-publish. Consequence to note: `@objectstack/spec` is in the fixed group, so the whole `@objectstack/*` group takes a minor bump.
- `.changeset/cloud-3383-chatbot-tool-label-draft-record.md`: `@object-ui/i18n` **patch**, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right: a display string in each pack, nothing an author writes; `@object-ui/i18n` is in the root `.changeset/config.json` fixed group, so the root changeset dir is the correct home.
- PR body carries the same two declaration lines, line-initial, matching the spec changeset. Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green.

Clause-②: yes (widening)

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author login is `os-zhuang` (the implementation claim is the project thread named in the PR body; Implemented-by below carries the branch).
- Human Minimum item 3 is unchecked (no local `pnpm lint`): answered by the head's check-runs, where Lint & Repo Gates, every scoped Lint lane, ESLint and Lint UI are green.
- No dev flag and no `open_questions` entry in the PR body. The Docs Drift Check's "checkout carried uncommitted changes" note describes the CI runner's merge checkout, not this diff; no action.
- Escalated, not blocking: the exact spelling `draft_record` and the "writes nothing" characterisation are facts about cloud#3383's registration, which this seat cannot read. The contract's enforcement for the name is the cloud conformance test (`platform-tool-names-conformance.test.ts`, per the registry header and ADR-0109): if cloud registers a different name, that test goes red in the cloud pin round, not here. #28104 names the RESULT status `record_draft` while the TOOL is `draft_record`; these are different things (a status value inside the tool result versus the tool name), not a contradiction, but the cloud pin round should confirm both spellings against the landed cloud tool.
- `check-runs` on the head: 64 runs, every required job success; the skipped ones (Temporal Conformance, Dogfood matrix lanes, UI Published Artifacts, Build Docs, opt-in harnesses, schedule gate) are path- or opt-in-filtered and owe nothing to this diff. Governed Surface Queue Guard and Spec property liveness are green.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts`, judged against ADR-0109 (the ruling it implements) and its first consumer `validateAiToolReferences`, with the chatbot parity test and the MCP bridge as the other two readers.

- Against ADR-0109 decision 2 ("platform tool names are facts, not guesses; the owning cloud packages carry conformance tests"): the maintenance contract in the file header says registering a tool in a cloud AI package means adding its name here, plus a `chatbot.tool.NAME` label in every pack. The diff does exactly those two things and nothing more. The registry stays a curated fact list; no runtime logic enters `packages/spec`.
- Against the first consumer: the resolution ladder reads the flattened set, so the one-line addition is the entire behaviour change, and the PR pins it with a positive case and a near-miss control in the rule's own test file, where "resolves" and "refused" are decided, not beside the constant. Tried to break it: a universe widened too far would pass the positive case and fail the control; a misplaced (unsorted) entry would fail the spec's sort pin; a missing pack entry would fail the parity test per pack. Each failure mode has a red gate on the head's file set.
- Against the scenario it is accepted for (cloud#3383 via the PR body and #28104): the ask agent emits a validated new-record draft the person saves. Registering a hand-off signal in `service-ai-studio` alongside `suggest_builder` and `open_record` follows the group these signals already live in; the PR body states cloud#3383 registers it in that package, and the cloud conformance test holds that package to exactly this group, so a wrong group would red the cloud side rather than pass silently.
- MCP side effect considered and found right (① above): `openWorldHint: false` for a tool that drafts a record of this stack's own object is the known answer the bridge wants; no safety hint is asserted without a source.
- Label texts: each pack's value is a sentence in its language, none equals the id or `Draft record`; alphabetical beside its neighbours in every pack. The ja, ko and zh values read as instructions to the user ("make a draft of the new record"), matching the ruled style (todo_write's sentence form).

Findings: no must-fix. No should-fix. The design holds against the code it cites and the gates that enforce it.
